citations.quote: A genuine single family office arrangement, established to serve the investment needs of members of a single family, which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective, should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.

readings.distinction: Three plausible constructions are shared negation, narrow negation with an affirmative second alternative, and two independently negative alternatives. This first construction requires both absences. The prior shared-negation and conjunctive-negation formulas are logically equivalent, so they do not supply distinct substantive readings. Shared negation is contextually preferable because the preceding sentence identifies profit-making purpose as a business indicator, but the irregular coordination does not settle the interpretation. No additional defensible Boolean reading absent from the prior hypotheses was identified.

vocabulary_concerns: The supplied income fact cannot distinguish the parenthetical income test from the broader case-specific assessment of being run as a business. Occupation or duty, continuity, and capability of profit are not represented. A reading treating the parenthetical as illustrative rather than exhaustive would therefore require null formalization under this vocabulary; it cannot be implemented by silently redefining the supplied fact.

The Boolean fragment does not express the qualified force of should not in the ordinary course or regulatory intent. These remain qualifications on the conclusion, not additional encoded antecedent conditions.
The genuine-family fact combines genuineness, single-family status, and investment-serving purpose. It cannot separately test those descriptions or determine family membership.

The three supplied facts cannot determine regulated activity, the intra-group carve-out, territorial scope, or a licensing obligation. Truth and falsity of these antecedent predicates establish neither exemption nor obligation.

The prior four expressions represent three Boolean conditions: negating a disjunction and conjoining the two negations are equivalent. Their separate presentation supplies no additional legal diversity.

No defensible additional attachment was identified that lets the profit-objective branch escape the genuine-single-family-office requirement. The regulatory-intent sentence likewise supplies no express alternative antecedent. These possibilities should not be added merely to increase diversity.
